## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #244 addresses issue #243 by disabling scheduled daily summaries by default while keeping manual dispatch available, and by raising default orchestration handoff rounds from 5 to 12. It updates workflow defaults, TypeScript CLI fallbacks, docs, and focused tests. The orchestration-round change looks consistently applied. The daily-summary default is incomplete for repositories that already set any custom `AGENT_SCHEDULE_POLICY`.

## Review

Overall, this needs rework before merge because a non-empty unrelated schedule policy can still re-enable the daily summary cron. The remaining test-coverage gap is lower risk but easy to fix alongside the blocking schedule-policy change.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Custom schedule policies can re-enable daily summaries | BLOCKING | The PR disables `agent-daily-summary.yml` only when `AGENT_SCHEDULE_POLICY` is empty; with any non-empty policy that omits that workflow, both gates fall back to `default_mode` and can run scheduled summaries. This conflicts with issue #243 and the updated docs that say the cron is disabled by default and enabled via a workflow override. |
| `orchestrate-handoff` fallback default lacks direct regression coverage | WARNING | The changed `orchestrate-handoff.ts` fallback from 5 to 12 has no new no-env test, while related dispatch/preflight fallbacks do. This is low risk because workflows pass the input explicitly, but the coverage is asymmetric. |

## Progress

- PR #244 already updates the 12-round default across workflows, dispatch CLIs, docs, and focused tests.
- Empty-policy daily-summary behavior and manual dispatch behavior are now tested.
- Rubrics review passed with no rubric-specific findings.
- Existing inline comments and review threads were empty before synthesis.
- Posted one inline comment for the blocking schedule-policy issue on `.agent/scripts/resolve-scheduled-activity-gate.sh` line 75.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Custom schedule policies can re-enable daily summaries</summary>

**Cause:** In the TypeScript parser, non-empty policies initialize `workflowOverrides` as `{}` instead of preserving defaults, so `agent-daily-summary.yml` falls back to `defaultMode`: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b8860718fb59f0fc06b98b47c4c2acbb134aa45a/.agent/src/schedule-policy.ts#L57-L60. The shell gate mirrors this by returning `$default_mode` when no matching override is present: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/b8860718fb59f0fc06b98b47c4c2acbb134aa45a/.agent/scripts/resolve-scheduled-activity-gate.sh#L121-L124.

**Candidate solutions:** Keep `agent-daily-summary.yml` disabled unless `workflow_overrides["agent-daily-summary.yml"]` explicitly opts into `skip_no_updates` or `always_run`. Mirror the behavior in both the TypeScript parser and shell pre-runtime gate, and add TS plus shell tests for a non-empty policy that only mentions another workflow.

**Comments:** One reviewer considered the asymmetry acceptable operator-control behavior, but the synthesis treats it as blocking because the issue request and docs describe disabled-by-default behavior with explicit workflow-override enablement.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`orchestrate-handoff` fallback default lacks direct regression coverage</summary>

**Cause:** `orchestrate-handoff.ts` changed its fallback to 12, but existing `orchestrate-handoff-cli.test.ts` cases set `AUTOMATION_MAX_ROUNDS` explicitly rather than covering the omitted-env fallback.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a focused CLI test that omits or clears `AUTOMATION_MAX_ROUNDS` and asserts the dispatched handoff payload uses `12`.

**Comments:** This is lower risk because `agent-orchestrator.yml` passes the defaulted workflow input, but direct fallback coverage would match the rest of the PR.

</details>

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: The blocking behavior and missing regression coverage are concrete branch changes that are safe for an automated fix-pr pass.

## Final Verdict

NEEDS_REWORK

## Action Items

- [ ] Keep `agent-daily-summary.yml` disabled for scheduled runs unless `AGENT_SCHEDULE_POLICY.workflow_overrides["agent-daily-summary.yml"]` explicitly enables it, in both TypeScript and shell gates.
- [ ] Add TypeScript and shell regression tests for a non-empty unrelated `AGENT_SCHEDULE_POLICY` that omits `agent-daily-summary.yml`.
- [ ] Add a focused no-env fallback regression test for `orchestrate-handoff.ts` defaulting `AUTOMATION_MAX_ROUNDS` to `12`.

@sepo-agent /answer

Wait a sec I merged this pr and then launched another implement request https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/250 but the title is still not correct ?

Yes, you’re right: #250 should not have kept the fallback title.

What happened:

- The title fix came from PR #232, not PR #244. PR #244 only changed daily-summary/orchestration defaults.
- The #250 router run did enter the new `Generate implement issue metadata` step.
- That metadata step failed before returning JSON. The log shows Codex tried to run `gh pr view 241 ...`, requested interactive network approval, then the workflow aborted it.
- Because the step is `continue-on-error`, `Resolve route` continued and logged: `Implement issue metadata was invalid; using fallback metadata`.
- So #250 was created with the fallback title: `Implement requested change`.

So this is a real bug in the new metadata path, not GitHub caching.

The fix should be: make the metadata step non-interactive. Either prefetch the PR/discussion context deterministically before invoking the agent, or adjust the metadata prompt/runtime so read-only GitHub context access does not require an interactive approval. The intended title for #250 would be something like:

`Replace skill setup manifest with setup.sh hook`

The issue body still contains the full request, so implementation can proceed, but the tracking issue title fallback behavior needs a follow-up fix.

> adjust the metadata prompt/runtime so read-only GitHub context access does not require an interactive approval

@sepo-agent /answer we should add a small fix? Also the gh view command should work right?

Yes, this should be a small fix.

The important distinction: `gh pr view ...` **does work** in the workflow shell with `GH_TOKEN`. The failure was not that `gh pr view` is impossible. It failed because the metadata prompt asked the **Codex tool runtime** to run `gh pr view`, and under `permission_mode: approve-reads` that still triggered an interactive “allow network command?” approval. In GitHub Actions there is nobody to approve it, so the metadata step got cancelled and Sepo fell back to `Implement requested change`.

I would not fix this by changing the metadata step to `approve-all`. Better small fix:

1. Keep the metadata agent read-only.
2. Fetch PR/discussion context deterministically before the agent prompt, using workflow/CLI code with `GH_TOKEN`.
3. Inject that fetched context into the metadata prompt.
4. Update `agent-implement-metadata.md` so it says “use the provided target context”, not “run `gh pr view` yourself.”
5. Add a regression asserting the metadata prompt path does not require agent tool approval for `gh pr view`.

So yes: `gh pr view` should work, but it should be run by the workflow/runtime before the agent call, not interactively by the metadata agent.
